title: Service install and lifecycle on Windows
description:
hire/src/main.rs:534 install_service() has a #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] branch writing a launchd plist and a Linux branch writing a systemd user unit. There is no Windows branch, and SPEC-HIRE's Windows user-mode service name was marked '(not implemented)' in the 2026-09-15 de-specification (commit eb72478) rather than removed, so it is a documented target with nothing behind it.

THE DECISION FIRST, THE CODE SECOND: hired is a USER-SESSION daemon. Its whole premise is 'who is the human at this keyboard', so it must run in the interactive user's session with access to that user's agents and tokens -- not as a LocalSystem service shared across sessions. A Windows service running as LocalSystem would be the wrong shape entirely: one instance, many sessions, and a pseudonym story that cannot work.

So the real options are a per-user scheduled task at logon, a startup entry, or a service that runs per-session. Decide which before writing installer code, and record why, the way the systemd unit and launchd plist decisions are recorded.

Note persona-5s4b.26 in passing: install_service() currently fights the compiler with two lint suppressions rather than cfg-gating the Linux branch. Adding a third platform to that shape makes it worse, so .26 is worth doing first or together.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision on how hired starts on Windows that preserves per-user-session isolation; installer code only after that; install_service() cfg-gated rather than lint-suppressed.
